COMPUTATIONAL MODELING OF THERMAL FIELD-FLOW FRACTIONATION: LIMITATIONS OF THE TALBOT MODEL FOR LIQUID-PHASE NANOFLUIDS
recent_works.abstract: The performance of nanofluids in thermal management systems is strongly influenced by thermodiffusion (Soret effect), which drives nanoparticle migration under temperature gradients and can lead to aggregation and property changes. This study employs a two-dimensional computational framework modeled after a Thermal Field-Flow Fractionation (ThFFF) channel to investigate thermophoretic transport in water-based nanofluids containing alumina, copper, and hybrid nanoparticles. Simulations were performed in ANSYS Fluent under a 50 K cross-stream gradient using two formulations: (i) the default Talbot model, based on ideal-gas assumptions, and (ii) a Buongiorno-based, property-dependent model implemented via a User-Defined Function (UDF). Results show that the Talbot model predicts cold-wall particle accumulation but fails to differentiate between particle materials or sizes, producing nearly identical concentration and residence-time profiles for all cases. recent_works.title: A Poro-Elastic Network Model Predicting Reactant Transport and Local Water Balance in PEMFC Electrodes
recent_works.abstract: A modeling tool for predicting reactant transport, electrochemical activity, and local water balance in PEMFC electrodes is presented. The network model architecture, in conjunction with poro-elastic swelling theory, is adapted to account for morphological changes in the electrodes. Local transport phenomena are analyzed by applying energy and mass balances to the network system, incorporating both liquid and vapor phase behaviors of water. This modeling technique is computationally efficient and effectively captures the microstructure of PEMFC electrodes under varying thermodynamic conditions, such as different fuel cell operating scenarios. Additionally, the model provides valuable insights into the interaction between transport properties and electrochemical performance, making it a versatile tool for optimizing PEMFC design and operation.
